license_note: The downloadable weights carry the Qwen Community License 1.0, which grants use, modification, distribution, hosting, and fine-tuning with attribution above 100 million monthly active users or 20 million US dollars in monthly revenue, but requires any model-as-a-service or AI-work-assistant business to obtain a separate license before any commercial use, with no revenue threshold. That stricter commercial gate distinguishes it from the Max sibling license, so the release is source-available rather than open source. The production qwen3.8-flash API service is governed separately.

license_evidence.scope: Model weights, parameters, configuration files, inference code, and associated documentation in the Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next repository; does not cover the hosted qwen3.8-flash API service

access_boundary: This record represents the fixed, dated Qwen3.8-Flash-Next preview checkpoint released August 26, 2026 as an early look at the Qwen4 architecture — a named reviewable artifact, not a floating tag. The production qwen3.8-flash API model, the Max flagship and its snapshots, the Apache-2.0 Qwen3.8-27B sibling, earlier Qwen generations, Qwen4 proper when it lands, and community quantizations remain separate boundaries.
strengths: First open-weight release of the Qwen4-track architecture with full model card, tech report, and SGLang, vLLM, and TokenSpeed recipes
Roughly one-ninth the training cost of the prior generation flagship at competitive coding and agent capability with 6B active parameters per token
tradeoffs: The Community 1.0 weights license forces any model-as-a-service or AI-assistant business into a separate license with no revenue floor
No inference provider or first-party API serves this exact checkpoint, so self-operation is the only path
